text: random question but why do we even get hiccups

text: how does a fridge actually keep things cold, like what's the mechanism

turns.content: It's a refrigeration cycle — a refrigerant gas gets compressed (heating it up) then pushed through coils outside the fridge where it dumps that heat and condenses to liquid, then it expands through a valve into the inside coils where it evaporates again, absorbing heat from the fridge's interior as it does. That cooled gas then goes back to the compressor and repeats.

notes: Pure general-knowledge/how-things-work question, correct behavior answers directly.

text: does salting pasta water actually do anything or is that just a thing people say

turns.content: It genuinely does something — it seasons the pasta itself as it cooks (water alone just rinses off), since the starch on the surface absorbs some salt. It has a negligible effect on boiling point, so it's really about flavour, not cook time.

notes: Pure general-knowledge question, correct behavior answers directly.

text: what's the actual difference between a virus and bacteria, like at a basic level

turns.content: Bacteria are full living cells that can reproduce on their own; viruses aren't considered fully alive — they're just genetic material in a protein shell that can only replicate by hijacking a host cell's machinery. That's also why antibiotics work on bacteria but not viruses.

notes: Pure general-knowledge question, correct behavior answers directly.

text: how do noise cancelling headphones actually work, is it just blocking sound physically

turns.content: There's a physical component (the ear cups sealing out sound), but the real trick is active noise cancellation — a microphone picks up the ambient noise, the headphones generate an inverted sound wave matching it, and the two waves cancel each other out before they reach your ear.

notes: Pure general-knowledge/how-things-work question, correct behavior answers directly.
